name: Koumiss
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: two ounces of baker's yeast or a cake of compressed yeast
ingredients.originalText: two ounces of baker's yeast or a cake of compressed yeast
ingredients.quantityText: two ounces of baker's yeast or a cake of compressed yeast

instructions.text: Dissolve four ounces of white sugar in one gallon of skimmed milk
Place in bottles of the capacity of one quart
Add two ounces of baker's yeast or a cake of compressed yeast to each bottle
Set in a warm place until fermentation is well under way
Lay the bottles on their sides in a cool cellar
In three days, fermentation will have progressed sufficiently to permit the koumiss to be in good condition

source.author: F.L. Gillette
source.originalInstructions:
1. Dissolve four ounces of white sugar in one gallon of skimmed milk
2. Place in bottles of the capacity of one quart
3. Add two ounces of baker's yeast or a cake of compressed yeast to each bottle
4. Cork and tie securely
5. Set in a warm place until fermentation is well under way
6. Lay the bottles on their sides in a cool cellar
7. In three days, fermentation will have progressed sufficiently to permit the koumiss to be in good condition
